tally.headline: 6 of 12 gradeable claims held up, 5 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 3.7 points toward Baltimore Ravens of the quote EdgeDesk captured at Caesars. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 47.2 sat 3.7 points above the captured total of 43.5.

closing_line.note: The line moved 0.3 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 5 of 10 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — 1 defensive touchdown — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a away margin of 0.2 and the game finished 7 the away way — 6.8 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: 1 defensive touchdown
variance_markers.text: A defensive score puts points on the board that no offensive rating predicted and no offensive rating should be graded on.

variance_markers.label: 1 non-offensive or return score
variance_markers.text: Points that arrived without an offensive drive. They count the same on the scoreboard and belong to a different distribution from the one the model prices.

verdict.line: THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a win. The reasoning behind it did not hold: 5 of 10 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
lessons.lesson: A winning number built on a reading the game contradicted. Nothing about this result should increase confidence in the mechanism EdgeDesk named, and treating it as confirmation is how a model gets worse while its record gets better.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Why did the number land while the mechanism failed? Either the number was right for a reason EdgeDesk has not identified, or it was luck. Both are worth knowing and they are different.
